messages.subject: Covariances results
parts:
Hello
I have a question about the covariances results when running cfa(). The results from Lavaan are not exactly as the covariances results from Amos, but everything else are the same such as correlations, standardized regressions between latent variables and observations, and model fit indicators.  I am a bit confused that if a correlation is calculated based on covariance and SD, how can the covariances results but being the same but lead to a same correlation result?
Thank you
Xiguang Liu

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Covariances results
parts:
Not scaling of the covariances, but of the variances of the latents. The variance of a latent is undefined without an additional constraint. There are multiple ways to impose the constraint. cfa() by default (you didn't show us your function call) does so by fixing the loading of the first indicator of each latent to 1. I don't have direct knowledge of what AMOS does, but the other common standard in CFAs is to constrain the latent's variance to 1.

You can look to the variances sections of your output to see this.

The resulting models are equivalent.

messages.author: 515b030b2cb5ea36
messages.subject: Re: Covariances results
parts: What you have going on in that you have to set a scale to identify a latent variable. Usually that means that you either set the first indicators factor loading to 1 or set the variance of the latent variable to 1. If you set the variance of the latent variable to 1, then that latent variables is standardized. If you did that in Amos, but in Lavaan did it differently, the covariances would be different, but the correlations would be the same. The reason why is that the correlations come from the standardized solution which is setting the variances of the latent variables to 1. So make sure that in both Amos and Lavaan that in the covariances or unstandardized solution that the first factor loading is set to 1 (default in both) and the factor variances are freely estimated. That should fix it.
